raw_response:
**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father did wheat and corn, I do wheat and corn, and I'll keep doing wheat and corn. The North China Plain is made for this rotation — wheat in winter, corn in summer, same 8 mu of irrigated land. I have no reason to change.

At 60, I'm not experimenting. My knees aren't what they were, so I appreciate rotary tillage — it's fast and my son-in-law can help operate the machine we share with the village. No-till sounds good but I don't trust it; I've seen weeds get out of hand with neighbors who tried it.

For wheat, I buy the Jimai 22 seeds from the township supply station like always — it's an improved variety I know, decent yield, not too tall so it doesn't lodge. For corn, hybrid is just standard now, I get Xianyu 335 or whatever the co-op recommends that's similar.

Fertilizer: I put on what the county extension office told us years ago, maybe a bit more because my soil feels tired lately. I'll apply urea at planting and again at jointing for wheat, base compound fertilizer for corn then topdress once.

Irrigation: I pull from the village well system. Wheat needs water at jointing and heading for sure, I usually do 3 rounds total across the season. Corn in summer gets rain mostly, but I'll irrigate once if July is dry like last year.

Pesticides: herbicide early for wheat, spray for rust or powdery mildew if I see it in spring. Corn gets one herbicide pass and I watch for armyworm.
